problems.problem: The Step 3 question asks Uday to judge 'the reviews and the coverage draft shown above', but they are three replies back in msg 20 and are not repeated. The user says he would not scroll for them, so he is asked to decide on material he cannot see.
problems.cause: The prompt rule 'Never repeat a table, list, search or explanation already shown in this session; refer to it in a few words' beats 'whatever a question asks the team to judge is in the same reply'. The early move (msg 20) showed the results under a certification ask, long before the Step 3 question.
problems.fix: Add to 'Files and pace': 'This overrides never-repeat: when Your turn asks the team to judge results shown in an earlier reply, repeat their compact form in that reply (the FACT lines, the coverage DRAFT in at most four lines, and up to five table rows).'

problems.problem: One reply holds six full search cards (two of them full-length variant strings), two results tables, the coverage DRAFT, an 18-entry Sources line and the TP certification. Prose is about 280-344 words against the 180-word limit. The user called it a 'very long wall of text' and asked for the strategy again.
problems.cause: 'Moving ahead' says to 'do the most useful work the rules allow' but does not limit what an early reply shows while an earlier certification still blocks. Each variant and each OpenAlex duplicate also needs a full card.
problems.fix: Add to 'Moving ahead': 'While an earlier certification is open, the early reply shows only the one-line move, the FACT lines, the search cards, what is not yet searched, and the certification line; results tables and drafts wait for the reply that asks the team to judge them (one line under Next).'

problems.problem: The results table column 'People named (words found)' drops 'type 2 diabetes' whenever 'without diabetes' also matched (_people() in env/stir_l4_local.py, lines 286-294). 4 of the 10 rows (PMIDs 42215421, 42011503, 36931466, 34542222) therefore look like reviews in people without diabetes only, though their abstracts also name type 2 diabetes. The table also has no supporting passage per row.
problems.cause: The agent wrote its own 346-line helper and table instead of using k.review_table, which quotes a passage for each row. The kit's table accepts only PubMed fetch records and one term list, so it could not handle pooled PubMed and OpenAlex rows (K1: 346 helper lines and 65 notebook lines).
problems.fix: Kit: extend k.review_table to accept pooled PubMed and OpenAlex rows and several named term groups, list every group matched, and keep the quoted-passage column. Prompt 3.10: 'Build every results table with k.review_table; a column of matched terms lists every group found, never a subset.'

problems.problem: The Team's Purpose DRAFT says 'Added by me: nothing', but its wording includes 'within the whole topic', which is the agent's reading of Uday's bare 'yes' to a two-part item. The reading is disclosed in the same line, but the 'nothing' claim is not strictly true.
problems.cause: Prompt 2b says to 'ask once whether it holds within the whole topic' and that the statement names 'the whole topic, if the team says so'. It gives no rule for an unanswered either-or.
problems.fix: Add to 2b: 'If the whole-topic question is left unanswered, leave the scope out of the purpose wording, or write "Added by me: within the whole topic (my reading of your yes)"; never pair an inference with "Added by me: nothing".'

problems.problem: Two of the three numbered items each ask two things (1: yes/edit plus whole-or-part; 3: a/b/c plus whether the publishing fit is wrong), and two option tables come before them. The terse user replied 'yes. 2 3. yes', which left the scope and the meaning of 'learning' open. The agent then included both learning kinds, and the log entry L000036 records them as 'Chose: ...' with actor Uday, although he chose neither.
problems.cause: Prompt 2b asks for 'one reply' covering the reflection, scope, purpose numbers and motivation fit. k.confirm_states attributes the states to the member even when the agent inferred them.
problems.fix: In 2b, make scope an option within item 1 ('1. Focus: a yes, whole topic; b yes, only part (say which); c edit'), and show the publishing fit only in the DRAFT table, not as a question. Kit: k.confirm_states(..., inferred=True) logs actor 'agent (draft)' until certification.

problems.problem: The move-ahead line ('Moved to Step 3 as you asked; searched PubMed and OpenAlex for reviews and protocols') does not say that Team's Purpose stays a draft, which the persona's pass criterion requires. It also implies OpenAlex was searched for protocols. Your turn has no example reply.
problems.cause: The prompt asks for 'one line ... what stays open', but k.early returns no ready-made line, and k.check_reply does not check for one or for a missing example.
problems.fix: Kit: k.early(step, open_items) returns md such as 'Moving to Step 3 early; Team's Purpose stays a draft until you certify it.' to be used as the Done line. k.check_reply flags a reply after k.early that lacks this line or has a Your turn without an example.

problems.problem: Done says 'This may change the Individual Motivation you approved, because the agreed purpose in turn shapes what each member seeks'. This is a weak flow, and the new purpose is consistent with the motivation. The user did not know whether he had to act.
problems.cause: The prompt's Done rule (R4) requires 'This may change the <decision> you approved' for any flow that reaches a certified decision, whether or not the new decision conflicts with it.
problems.fix: Change the Done rule to: 'If the new decision agrees with the certified one it reaches, write "Your <decision> still fits; nothing to do". Write "This may change ..." only when the new wording conflicts with or adds to what was certified, and then ask one question about it.'

problems.problem: Several terms are used without a gloss: PMID (prose and table header), DOI (coverage DRAFT), and Cochrane and Epistemonikos (msg 20, and again in the prose at msg 22). This brings plain-language M6 down to 1.

problems.problem: The first planning reply shows the full 12-row plan map, a labels legend and the quick commands before the one topic question. Msg 8 then repeats the full map. The persona's pass expected 'the topic question only', and the user said he skimmed it.

problems.fix: Prompt, Plan map: 'In the first planning reply show the status line, the one-sentence explanation and the topic question only; show the full map, labels and quick commands for the first time when the topic is recorded.'

problems.problem: The saved report reports/2026-10-25_S1_summary.md says 'Folders changed: env, log', but plan, data, notebooks and reports also changed this session. session.json has start_head set to the literal 'HEAD'. The false statement is in a saved record, not in the chat.
problems.cause: In the kit, _git_head() (lines 694-698) returns the stdout of 'git rev-parse HEAD'. On an empty repo at init that stdout is 'HEAD', so session_summary diffs against the latest commit instead of the session start.
problems.fix: Kit: in _git_head, check the returncode and return None when there is no commit. In session_summary, diff against the empty-tree hash 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 when start_head is None, or derive the folders from the session's log raw_path and derived_path values.
